subject: Chemistry
title: Marie Curie Discovers Radium
description: A short lesson to help you apply Marie Curie Discovers Radium.

hook.text: Marie Curie processed eight tons of pitchblende ore by hand to isolate one-tenth of a gram of radium.

buildup.text: She noticed that uranium ore was more radioactive than pure uranium. Something else must be hiding inside.

discovery.text: In 1898, she and Pierre isolated two new elements: polonium (named for Poland) and radium ('ray').

twist.text: Radium glowed blue in the dark. People put it in paint, water, and even toothpaste before knowing the danger.

climax.text: Curie won two Nobel Prizes—the only person to win in two different sciences. She died of radiation exposure.

punchline.text: Eight tons of ore, one-tenth of a gram. Two Nobel Prizes.

quiz.question: How did Curie realize there were unknown elements in uranium ore?
options: The ore was more radioactive than pure uranium alone could explain
The ore glowed in the dark
The ore was heavier than expected

details.summary: Marie Curie discovered radium in 1898 by processing tons of uranium ore residue, observing that residues were more radioactive than pure uranium. She coined the term radioactivity and isolated radium through exhausting chemical separation, winning Nobel Prizes in both physics and chemistry.
details.whyItMatters: Curie's discovery revealed that atoms are not indivisible and can spontaneously transform, overturning fundamental assumptions. Radium launched nuclear physics and led to cancer treatment through radiation therapy.
takeaways: Curie processed tons of pitchblende ore to isolate tiny amounts of radium
She coined the term radioactivity to describe spontaneous atomic emission
Curie remains the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences

faq.question: How did Curie determine that the ore contained an unknown radioactive element?
faq.answer: Curie measured that pitchblende ore was four times more radioactive than the uranium it contained. Since no known element could account for the excess radioactivity, she deduced that an unknown, highly radioactive element must be present..

faq.question: What health consequences did Curie suffer from her radiation exposure?
faq.answer: Curie developed aplastic anemia from years of radiation exposure and died in 1934 at age 66. She carried radioactive materials in her pockets and stored them in her desk drawer. Her personal belongings, including notebooks, remain radioactive and are kept in lead-lined boxes..
